 31534                                  ;Break	<MAPCLUSTER - BUFFER A FAT SECTOR>
 31535                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31536                                  ;
 31537                                  ; Procedure Name : MAPCLUSTER
 31538                                  ;
 31539                                  ; Inputs:
 31540                                  ;	ES:BP Points to DPB
 31541                                  ;	BX Is cluster number
 31542                                  ; Function:
 31543                                  ;	Get a pointer to the cluster
 31544                                  ; Outputs:
 31545                                  ;	DS:DI Points to contents of FAT for given cluster
 31546                                  ;	DS:SI Points to start of buffer
 31547                                  ;	Zero Not set if cluster data is in high 12 bits of word
 31548                                  ;	Zero set if cluster data is in low 12 or 16 bits
 31549                                  ;	Carry set if failed.
 31550                                  ; SI is destroyed.
 31551                                  ;
 31552                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31553                                  
 31554                                  	; 20/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 31555                                  	; DOSCODE:9601h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 31556                                  	; 27/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 31557                                  	; DOSCODE:95A5h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
 31558                                  
 31559                                  MAPCLUSTER:
 31560                                  	; IBMDOS.COM (MSDOS 3.3, 1987) - Offset 5A15h
 31561 0000548E C606[7805]00            	MOV	BYTE [CLUSSPLIT],0
 31562                                  	;SAVE	<AX,BX,CX,DX>
 31563 00005493 50                      	push	ax
 31564 00005494 53                      	push	bx
 31565 00005495 51                      	push	cx
 31566 00005496 52                      	push	dx
 31567 00005497 89D8                    	MOV	AX,BX			; AX = BX
 31568 00005499 26817E0DF60F            	CMP	word [ES:BP+DPB.MAX_CLUSTER],4096-10  ; MZ 16 bit fat?
 31569 0000549F 7302                    	JAE	short Map16		; MZ yes, do 16 bit algorithm
 31570 000054A1 D1E8                    	SHR	AX,1			; AX = BX/2
 31571                                  Map16:	
 31572                                  	; MSDOS 6.0			; MZ skip prev => AX=2*BX
 31573 000054A3 31FF                    	XOR	DI,DI ; *		; >32mb fat ;AN000;
 31574                                  	; MSDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)
 31575 000054A5 01D8                    	ADD	AX,BX			; AX = 1.5*fat = byte offset in fat
 31576 000054A7 11FF                    	ADC	DI,DI ; * MSDOS 6.0	; >32mb fat ;DI is zero before op;AN000;
 31577 000054A9 268B4E02                	MOV	CX,[ES:BP+DPB.SECTOR_SIZE]
 31578                                  
 31579                                  ;IF FastDiv
 31580                                  ;
 31581                                  ; Gross hack: 99% of all disks have 512 bytes per sector. We test for this
 31582                                  ; case and apply a really fast algorithm to get the desired results
 31583                                  ;
 31584                                  ; Divide method takes 157+4*4=173 (MOV and DIV)
 31585                                  ; Fast method takes 39+20*4=119
 31586                                  ;
 31587                                  ; This saves a bunch.
 31588                                  
 31589 000054AD 81F90002                	CMP	CX,512			; 4  Is this 512 byte sector?
 31590 000054B1 7510                    	jne	short _DoDiv		; 4  for no jump
 31591 000054B3 89C2                    	MOV	DX,AX			; 2  get set for remainder
 31592 000054B5 81E2FF01                	AND	DX,512-1		; 4  Form remainder
 31593 000054B9 88E0                    	MOV	AL,AH			; 2  Quotient in formation in AL
 31594                                  	; MDOS 3.3
 31595                                  	;shr	al,1	
 31596                                  	; MDOS 6.0
 31597 000054BB D1EF                    	shr	di,1			; 2
 31598 000054BD D0D8                    	rcr	al,1			; 2
 31599                                  	; MDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)
 31600 000054BF 30E4                    	xor	ah,ah			; 3
 31601 000054C1 EB04                    	jmp	short DivDone		; 16
 31602                                  _DoDiv:
 31603                                  ;ENDIF
 31604                                  	; MSDOS 3.3
 31605                                  	;xor	dx,dx
 31606                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 31607 000054C3 89FA                    	mov	dx,di			; 2
 31608                                  	; MSDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)	
 31609 000054C5 F7F1                    	DIV	CX			; 155 AX is FAT sector # DX is sector index

 31712                                  ; Procedure Name : FATREAD_SFT
 31713                                  ;
 31714                                  ; Inputs:
 31715                                  ;	ES:DI points to an SFT for the drive of intrest (local only,
 31716                                  ;		giving a NET SFT will produce system crashing results).
 31717                                  ;	DS DOSDATA
 31718                                  ; Function:
 31719                                  ;	Can be used by an SFT routine (like CLOSE) to invalidate buffers
 31720                                  ;	if disk changed.
 31721                                  ;	In other respects, same as FATREAD_CDS.
 31722                                  ;	(note ES:DI destroyed!)

 31724                                  ;	Carry set if error (currently user FAILed to I 24)
 31725                                  ; NOTE: This routine may cause FATREAD_CDS to "miss" a disk change
 31726                                  ;	as far as invalidating curdir_ID is concerned.
 31727                                  ;	Since getting a true disk changed on this call is a screw up
 31728                                  ;	anyway, that's the way it goes.
 31729                                  ;

 32641                                  ;**	GetBuffr - Get a non-FAT Sector into a Buffer
 32642                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 32643                                  ;	GetBuffr does normal ( non-FAT ) sector buffering
 32644                                  ;	It gets the specified local sector into one of the I/O buffers
 32645                                  ;	and shuffles the queue
 32646                                  ; 
 32647                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = 0 means sector must be pre-read
 32648                                  ;		       ELSE no pre-read
 32649                                  ;		(DX) = Desired physical sector number	      (LOW)
 32650                                  ;		HIGH_SECTOR = Desired physical sector number (HIGH)
 32651                                  ;		(ES:BP) = Pointer to drive parameters
 32652                                  ;		ALLOWED set in case of INT 24
 32653                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error (user FAIL response to INT24)
 32654                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 32655                                  ;		CURBUF Points to the Buffer for the sector
 32656                                  ;		    the buffer type bits OF buf_flags = 0, caller must set it
 32657                                  ;	USES	AX, BX, CX, SI, DI, Flags
 32658                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 32659                                  
 32660                                  ;**	GetBuffrb - Get a FAT Sector into a Buffer
 32661                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 32662                                  ;	GetBuffrb reads a sector from the FAT file system's FAT table.
 32663                                  ;	It gets the specified sector into one of the I/O buffers
 32664                                  ;	and shuffles the queue. We need a special entry point so that
 32665                                  ;	we can read the alternate FAT sector if the first read fails, also
 32666                                  ;	so we can mark the buffer as a FAT sector.
 32667                                  ; 
 32668                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = 0 means sector must be pre-read
 32669                                  ;		       ELSE no pre-read
 32670                                  ;		(DX) = Desired physical sector number	     (LOW)
 32671                                  ;		(SI) != 0
 32672                                  ;		HIGH_SECTOR = Desired physical sector number (HIGH)
 32673                                  ;		(ES:BP) = Pointer to drive parameters
 32674                                  ;		ALLOWED set in case of INT 24
 32675                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error (user FAIL response to INT24)
 32676                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 32677                                  ;		CUR ddBUF Points to the Buffer for the sector
 32678                                  ;		    the buffer type bits OF buf_flags = 0, caller must set it
 32679                                  ;	USES	AX, BX, CX, SI, DI, Flags

 33430                                  
 33431                                  ;	TITLE	MSPROC - process maintenance
 33432                                  ;	NAME	MSPROC
 33433                                  
 33434                                  ; =========================================================================
 33435                                  ;**	Process related system calls and low level routines for DOS 2.X.
 33436                                  ;	I/O specs are defined in DISPATCH.
 33437                                  ;
 33438                                  ;	$WAIT
 33439                                  ;	$EXEC
 33440                                  ;	$Keep_process
 33441                                  ;	Stay_resident
 33442                                  ;	$EXIT
 33443                                  ;	$ABORT
 33444                                  ;	abort_inner
 33445                                  ;
 33446                                  ;	Modification history:
 33447                                  ;
 33448                                  ;		Created: ARR 30 March 1983
 33449                                  ;		AN000	version 4.0 jan. 1988
 33450                                  ;		A007	PTM 3957 - fake vesrion for IBMCACHE.COM
 33451                                  ;		A008	PTM 4070 - fake version for MS WINDOWS
 33452                                  ;
 33453                                  ;		M000	added support for loading programs into UMBs 7/9/90
 33454                                  ;
 33455                                  ;		M004 - MS PASCAL 3.2 support. Please see under tag M003 in 
 33456                                  ;		       dossym.inc. 7/30/90
 33457                                  ;		M005 - Support for EXE programs with out STACK segment and 
 33458                                  ;		       with resident size < 64K - 256 bytes. A 256 byte 
 33459                                  ;		       stack is provided at the end of the program. Note that
 33460                                  ;		       only SP is changed.
 33461                                  ;		M020 - Fix for Rational bug for details see exepatch.asm
 33462                                  ;
 33463                                  ;		M028 - 4b04 implementation
 33464                                  ;
 33465                                  ;		M029 - Support for EXEs without stack rewritten. If EXE is
 33466                                  ;			in memory block >= 64K, sp = 0. If memory block
 33467                                  ;			obtained is <64K, point sp at the end of the memory
 33468                                  ;			block. For EXEs smaller than 64K, 256 bytes are still
 33469                                  ;			added for a stack segment which may be needed if it
 33470                                  ;			is loaded in low memory situations.
 33471                                  ;
 33472                                  ;		M030 - Fixing bug in EXEPACPATCH & changing 4b04 to 4b05
 33473                                  ;
 33474                                  ;		M040 - Bug #3052. The environment sizing code would flag a
 33475                                  ;			a bad environment if it reached 32767 bytes. Changed
 33476                                  ;			to allow 32768 bytes of environment.
 33477                                  ;
 33478                                  ;		M047 - Release the allocated UMB when we failed to load a 
 33479                                  ;		       COM file high. Also ensure that if the biggest block
 33480                                  ;		       into which we load the com file is less than 64K then
 33481                                  ;		       we provide atleast 256 bytes of stack to the user.
 33482                                  ;
 33483                                  ;		M050 - Made Lie table search CASE insensitive
 33484                                  ;
 33485                                  ;		M060 - Removed special version table from the kernal and
 33486                                  ;                      put it in a device drive which puts the address

 33537                                  ; =========================================================================
 33538                                  ;BREAK <$exec - load/go a program>
 33539                                  ;	EXEC.ASM - EXEC System Call
 33540                                  ;
 33541                                  ;
 33542                                  ; Assembler usage:
 33543                                  ;	    lds     DX, Name
 33544                                  ;	    les     BX, Blk
 33545                                  ;	    mov     AH, Exec
 33546                                  ;	    mov     AL, FUNC
 33547                                  ;	    int     INT_COMMAND
 33548                                  ;
 33549                                  ;	AL  Function
 33550                                  ;	--  --------
 33551                                  ;	 0  Load and execute the program.
 33552                                  ;	 1  Load, create the program header but do not
 33553                                  ;	    begin execution.
 33554                                  ;	 3  Load overlay. No header created.
 33555                                  ;
 33556                                  ;	    AL = 0 -> load/execute program
 33557                                  ;
 33558                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33559                                  ;	    | WORD segment address of	|
 33560                                  ;	    | environment.		|
 33561                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33562                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to ASCIZ	|
 33563                                  ;	    | command line at 80h	|
 33564                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33565                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33566                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 5Ch	|
 33567                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33568                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33569                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 6Ch	|
 33570                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33571                                  ;
 33572                                  ;	    AL = 1 -> load program
 33573                                  ;
 33574                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33575                                  ;	    | WORD segment address of	|
 33576                                  ;	    | environment.		|
 33577                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33578                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to ASCIZ	|
 33579                                  ;	    | command line at 80h	|
 33580                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33581                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33582                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 5Ch	|
 33583                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33584                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33585                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 6Ch	|
 33586                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33587                                  ;	    | DWORD returned value of	|
 33588                                  ;	    | CS:IP			|
 33589                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33590                                  ;	    | DWORD returned value of	|
 33591                                  ;	    | SS:IP			|
 33592                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33593                                  ;
 33594                                  ;	    AL = 3 -> load overlay
 33595                                  ;
 33596                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33597                                  ;	    | WORD segment address where|
 33598                                  ;	    | file will be loaded.	|
 33599                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33600                                  ;	    | WORD relocation factor to |
 33601                                  ;	    | be applied to the image.	|
 33602                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33603                                  ;
 33604                                  ; Returns:
 33605                                  ;	    AX = error_invalid_function
 33606                                  ;	       = error_bad_format
 33607                                  ;	       = error_bad_environment
 33608                                  ;	       = error_not_enough_memory
 33609                                  ;	       = error_file_not_found

 35328                                  ;BREAK <$ABORT -- Terminate a process>
 35329                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35330                                  ; Inputs:
 35331                                  ;	user_CS:00 must point to valid program header block
 35332                                  ; Function:
 35333                                  ;	Restore terminate and Cntrl-C addresses, flush buffers and transfer
 35334                                  ;	to the terminate address

 35336                                  ;	TO THE TERMINATE ADDRESS
 35337                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35338                                  
 35339                                  _$ABORT:

 35344

 35346                                  	; is retrieved from exit_type. Also, the PDB at user_CS needs
 35347                                  	; to be correct as the one that is terminating.
 35348

 35556                                  ;**	Arena_Next - Find Next item in Arena
 35557                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35558                                  ;	ENTRY	DS - pointer to block head
 35559                                  ;		(di) = 0
 35560                                  ;	EXIT	AX,ES - pointers to next head
 35561                                  ;		'C' set iff arena damaged

 35564                                  arena_next:
 35565 000060B3 8CD8                            MOV     AX,DS                   ; AX <- current block
 35566 000060B5 03060300                        ADD     AX,[ARENA.SIZE]		; AX <- AX + current block length
 35567 000060B9 40                              INC     AX                      ; remember that header!
 35568                                  
 35569                                  ;       fall into check_signature and return
 35570                                  ;
 35571                                  ;       CALL    check_signature         ; ES <- AX, carry set if error
 35572                                  ;       RETN

 35574                                  ;**	Check_Signature - Check Memory Block Signature
 35575                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35576                                  ;	ENTRY	(AX) = address of block header
 35577                                  ;		(di) = 0
 35578                                  ;	EXIT	 ES = AX

 35603                                  ;**	Coalesce - Combine free blocks ahead with current block
 35604                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35605                                  ;	Coalesce adds the block following the argument to the argument block,
 35606                                  ;	iff it's free.  Coalesce is usually used to join free blocks, but
 35607                                  ;	some callers (such as $setblock) use it to join a free block to it's
 35608                                  ;	preceeding allocated block.
 35609                                  ;
 35610                                  ;	ENTRY	(ds) = pointer to the head of a free block
 35611                                  ;		(di) = 0
 35612                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 35613                                  ;		  (ds) unchanged, this block updated
 35614                                  ;		  (ax) = address of next block, IFF not at end
 35615                                  ;		'C' set if arena trashed
 35616                                  ;	USES	(cx)
 35617                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35618                                          
 35619                                  Coalesce:
 35620                                  	;cmp	byte [di],5Ah ; 'Z'
 35621 000060CA 803D5A                  	CMP     BYTE [DI],arena_signature_end
 35622                                                                          ; IF current signature = END THEN
 35623                                          ;retz				;   GOTO ok
 35624 000060CD 74FA                            jz	short COALESCE_RETN
 35625 000060CF E8E1FF                  	CALL    arena_next              ; ES, AX <- next block, Carry set if error
 35626                                          ;retc				; IF no error THEN GOTO check
 35627 000060D2 72F5                    	jc	short COALESCE_RETN
 35628                                  
 35629                                  coalesce_check:
 35630                                  	;cmp	[es:1],di
 35631 000060D4 26393E0100                      CMP     [ES:ARENA.OWNER],DI
 35632                                          ;retnz				; IF next block isnt free THEN return
 35633 000060D9 75EE                            JNZ	SHORT COALESCE_RETN
 35634                                  	;mov	cx,[ES:3]
 35635 000060DB 268B0E0300              	MOV     CX,[ES:ARENA.SIZE]	; CX <- next block size
 35636 000060E0 41                              INC     CX                      ; CX <- CX + 1 (for header size)
 35637                                          ;ADD	[3],CX
 35638 000060E1 010E0300                	ADD     [ARENA.SIZE],CX		; current size <- current size + CX
 35639 000060E5 268A0D                          MOV     CL,[ES:DI]              ; move up signature
 35640 000060E8 880D                            MOV     [DI],CL
 35641 000060EA EBDE                            JMP     SHORT Coalesce		; try again

 35643                                  ; 04/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 35644                                  ; IBMDOS.COM (MSDOS 3.3, 1987) - Offset 641Fh
 35645                                  
 35646                                  ;	BREAK  <$Alloc - allocate space in memory>
 35647                                  
 35648                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 35649                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35650                                  ;**	$Alloc - Allocate Memory Space
 35651                                  ;
 35652                                  ;	$Alloc services the INT21 that allocates memory space to a program.
 35653                                  ;	Alloc returns a pointer to a free block of memory that
 35654                                  ;	has the requested size in paragraphs.
 35655                                  ;
 35656                                  ;	If the allocation strategy is HIGH_FIRST or HIGH_ONLY memory is 
 35657                                  ;	scanned from umb_head if not from arena_head. If the strategy is
 35658                                  ; 	HIGH_FIRST the scan is continued from arena_head if a block of 
 35659                                  ;	appropriate size is not found in the UMBs. If the strategy is 
 35660                                  ;	HIGH_FIRST+HIGH_ONLY only the UMBs are scanned for memory.
 35661                                  ;
 35662                                  ;	In either case if bit 0 of UmbFlag is not initialized then the scan
 35663                                  ;	starts from arena_head.
 35664                                  ;
 35665                                  ;	Assembler usage:
 35666                                  ;           MOV     BX,size
 35667                                  ;           MOV     AH,Alloc
 35668                                  ;           INT     21h
 35669                                  ;
 35670                                  ;	BUGBUG - a lot can be done to improve performance. We can set marks
 35671                                  ;	so that we start searching the arena at it's first non-trivial free
 35672                                  ;	block, we can peephole the code, etc. (We can move some subr calls
 35673                                  ;	inline, etc.) I assume that this is called rarely and that the arena
 35674                                  ;	doesn't have too many memory objects in it beyond the first free one.
 35675                                  ;	verify that this is true; if so, this can stay as is
 35676                                  ;
 35677                                  ;	ENTRY	(bx) = requested size, in bytes
 35678                                  ;		(DS) = (ES) = DOSGROUP
 35679                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if memory allocated
 35680                                  ;		  (ax:0) = address of requested memory
 35681                                  ;		'C' set if request failed
 35682                                  ;		  (AX) = error_not_enough_memory
 35683                                  ;		    (bx) = max size we could have allocated
 35684                                  ;		  (ax) = error_arena_trashed
 35685                                  ;	USES	All
 35686                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35687                                  
 35688                                  ; MSDOS 2.11 (& MSDOS 3.3)
 35689                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35690                                  ;SUBTTL $Alloc - allocate space in memory
 35691                                  ;
 35692                                  ;   Assembler usage:
 35693                                  ;           MOV     BX,size
 35694                                  ;           MOV     AH,Alloc
 35695                                  ;           INT     21h
 35696                                  ;         AX:0 is pointer to allocated memory
 35697                                  ;         BX is max size if not enough memory
 35698                                  ;
 35699                                  ;   Description:
 35700                                  ;           Alloc returns  a  pointer  to  a  free  block of
 35701                                  ;       memory that has the requested  size  in  paragraphs.
 35702                                  ;
 35703                                  ;   Error return:
 35704                                  ;           AX = error_not_enough_memory
 35705                                  ;              = error_arena_trashed
 35706                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35707                                  
 35708                                  ; DOSCODE:A28Eh (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 35709

 36046                                  ;	BREAK $SETBLOCK - change size of an allocated block (if possible)
 36047                                  
 36048                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 36049                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36050                                  ;**	$SETBLOCK - Change size of an Allocated Block
 36051                                  ;
 36052                                  ;	Setblock changes the size of an allocated block. First, we coalesce
 36053                                  ;	any following free space onto this block; then we try to trim the
 36054                                  ;	block down to the size requested.
 36055                                  ;
 36056                                  ;	Note that if the guy wants to grow the block but that growth fails,
 36057                                  ;	we still go ahead and coalesce any trailing free blocks onto it.
 36058                                  ;	Thus the maximum-size-possible value that we return has already
 36059                                  ;	been allocated! This is a bug, dare we fix it? BUGBUG
 36060                                  ;
 36061                                  ;	NOTE - $SETBLOCK is in bed with $ALLOC and jumps into $ALLOC to
 36062                                  ;		finish it's work. For this reason we build the allocsf
 36063                                  ;		structure on the frame, to make us compatible with $ALLOCs
 36064                                  ;		code.
 36065                                  ;
 36066                                  ;	ENTRY	(es) = segment of old block
 36067                                  ;		(bx) = newsize
 36068                                  ;		(ah) = SETBLOCK
 36069                                  ;
 36070                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 36071                                  ;		'C' set if error
 36072                                  ;		  (ax) = error_invalid_block
 36073                                  ;		       = error_arena_trashed
 36074                                  ;		       = error_not_enough_memory
 36075                                  ;		       = error_invalid_function
 36076                                  ;		  (bx) = maximum size possible, iff (ax) = error_not_enough_memory
 36077                                  ;	USES	???? BUGBUG
 36078                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36079                                  
 36080                                  ; MSDOS 2.11 (& MSDOS 3.3)
 36081                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36082                                  ;SUBTTL $SETBLOCK - change size of an allocated block (if possible)
 36083                                  ;
 36084                                  ;   Assembler usage:
 36085                                  ;           MOV     ES,block
 36086                                  ;           MOV     BX,newsize
 36087                                  ;           MOV     AH,setblock
 36088                                  ;           INT     21h
 36089                                  ;         if setblock fails for growing, BX will have the maximum
 36090                                  ;         size possible
 36091                                  ;   Error return:
 36092                                  ;           AX = error_invalid_block
 36093                                  ;              = error_arena_trashed
 36094                                  ;              = error_not_enough_memory
 36095                                  ;              = error_invalid_function
 36096                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36097                                  
 36098                                  _$SETBLOCK:        
 36099                                  	; 04/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 36100                                  	;EnterCrit   critMem
 36101 0000623D E8A2B0                  	call	ECritMEM ; MSDOS 3.3 & MSDOS 6.0

 36192                                  ;	BREAK $AllocOper - get/set allocation mechanism
 36193                                  
 36194                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 36195                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36196                                  ;**	$AllocOper - Get/Set Allocation Mechanism
 36197                                  ;
 36198                                  ;	Assembler usage:
 36199                                  ;           MOV     AH,AllocOper
 36200                                  ;           MOV     BX,method
 36201                                  ;           MOV     AL,func
 36202                                  ;           INT     21h
 36203                                  ;
 36204                                  ;	ENTRY	
 36205                                  ;		(al) = 0
 36206                                  ;		  Get allocation Strategy in (ax)
 36207                                  ;
 36208                                  ;		(al) = 1, (bx) = method = zw0000xy
 36209                                  ;		  Set allocation strategy.
 36210                                  ;		   w  = 1  => HIGH_ONLY
 36211                                  ;		   z  = 1  => HIGH_FIRST
 36212                                  ;		   xy = 00 => FIRST_FIT
 36213                                  ;		      = 01 => BEST_FIT
 36214                                  ;		      = 10 => LAST_FIT
 36215                                  ;
 36216                                  ;		(al) = 2
 36217                                  ;		  Get UMB link state in (al)
 36218                                  ;
 36219                                  ;		(al) = 3
 36220                                  ;		  Set UMB link state
 36221                                  ;		   (bx) = 0 => Unlink UMBs
 36222                                  ;		   (bx) = 1 => Link UMBs
 36223                                  ;
 36224                                  ;
 36225                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 36226                                  ;
 36227                                  ;		 if (al) = 0
 36228                                  ;		  (ax) = existing method
 36229                                  ;		 if (al) = 1
 36230                                  ;		  Sets allocation strategy
 36231                                  ;		 if (al) = 2
 36232                                  ;		  (al) = 0 => UMBs not linked
 36233                                  ;		  (al) = 1 => UMBs linked in
 36234                                  ;		 if (al) = 3
 36235                                  ;		  Links/Unlinks the UMBs into DOS chain
 36236                                  ;
 36237                                  ;		'C' set if error
 36238                                  ;		  AX = error_invalid_function
 36239                                  ;
 36240                                  ;	Rev. M000 - added support for HIGH_FIRST in (al) = 1. 7/9/90
 36241                                  ; 	Rev. M003 - added functions (al) = 2 and (al) = 3. 7/18/90
 36242                                  ;	Rev. M009 - (al) = 3 will return 'invalid function' in ax if
 36243                                  ;		    umbhead has'nt been initialized by sysinit and 'trashed
 36244                                  ;		    arena' if an arena sig is damaged.
 36245                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36246                                  
 36247                                  ; MSDOS 2.11 (& MSDOS 3.3)
 36248                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 36452                                  ; Procedure Name : GetLastArena		-  M003
 36453                                  ;
 36454                                  ; Inputs	 : cx = umb_head
 36455                                  ;
 36456                                  ;
 36457                                  ; Outputs	 : If UMBs are linked
 36458                                  ;			ES = umb_head
 36459                                  ;			DS = arena before umb_head
 36460                                  ;		   else

 36462                                  ;			ES = next arena. will be umb_head if NC.
 36463                                  ;
 36464                                  ;		   CY if error
 36465                                  ;
 36466                                  ; Uses		 : DS, ES, DI, BX
 36467                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36468                                  
 36469                                  ; 14/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 36470                                  ; DOSCODE:A4D6h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)

 36959                                  ;	BREAK	<pJFNFromHandle - return pointer to JFN table entry>
 36960                                  
 36961                                  ;**	pJFNFromHandle - Translate Handle to Pointer to JFN
 36962                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36963                                  ;	pJFNFromHandle takes a file handle and turns that into a pointer to
 36964                                  ;	the JFN entry (i.e., to a byte holding the internal file handle #)
 36965                                  ;
 36966                                  ;	NOTE:
 36967                                  ;	  This routine is called from $CREATE_PROCESS_DATA_BLOCK which is called
 36968                                  ;	  at DOSINIT time with SS NOT DOSGROUP
 36969                                  ;
 36970                                  ;	ENTRY	(bx) = handle
 36971                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if ok
 36972                                  ;		  (es:di) = address of JFN value
 36973                                  ;		'C' set if error
 36974                                  ;		  (ax) = error code
 36975                                  ;	USES	AX, DI, ES, Flags
 36976                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36977                                  
 36978                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 36979                                  
 36980                                  pJFNFromHandle:
 36981                                  	; 05/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 36982                                  	;getdseg <es>			; es -> dosdata
 36983 000064A0 2E8E06[0700]            	mov	es,[cs:DosDSeg]
 36984                                  	
 36985                                  	;MOV	ES,[cs:CurrentPDB]	; get user process data block
 36986 000064A5 268E06[3003]            	mov	es,[es:CurrentPDB]
 36987                                  
 36988                                  	;cmp	bx,[ES:32h]
 36989 000064AA 263B1E3200              	CMP	BX,[ES:PDB.JFN_Length]	; is handle greater than allocated
 36990 000064AF 7204                    	JB	short pjfn10		; no, get offset
 36991                                  ReturnCarry_inv_hndl: ; 05/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 36992                                  	;mov	al,6
 36993 000064B1 B006                    	MOV     AL,error_invalid_handle ; appropriate error
 36994                                  ReturnCarry:
 36995 000064B3 F9                      	STC                             ; signal error
 36996 000064B4 C3                      	retn				; go back
 36997                                  pjfn10: 
 36998                                  	;les	di,[es:34h]
 36999 000064B5 26C43E3400              	LES	DI,[ES:PDB.JFN_Pointer]	; get pointer to beginning of table
 37000 000064BA 01DF                    	ADD	DI,BX			; add in offset, clear 'C'
 37001                                  	;clc
 37002                                  pJFNFromHandle_error:
 37003 000064BC C3                      	retn

 37005                                  ;BREAK <SFFromHandle - return pointer (or error) to SF entry from handle>
 37006                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37007                                  ;
 37008                                  ; Procedure Name : SFFromHandle
 37009                                  ;
 37010                                  ; SFFromHandle - Given a handle, get JFN and then index into SF table
 37011                                  ;
 37012                                  ;   Input:      BX has handle
 37013                                  ;   Output:     Carry Set
 37014                                  ;                   AX has error code
 37015                                  ;               Carry Reset
 37016                                  ;                   ES:DI has pointer to SF entry
 37017                                  ;   Registers modified: If error, AX,ES, else ES:DI
 37018                                  ; NOTE:
 37019                                  ;   This routine is called from $CREATE_PROCESS_DATA_BLOCK which is called
 37020                                  ;       at DOSINIT time with SS NOT DOSGROUP
 37021                                  ;
 37022                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37023                                  
 37024                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37025                                  
 37026                                  SFFromHandle:
 37027 000064BD E8E0FF                  	CALL	pJFNFromHandle		; get jfn pointer
 37028                                  	;retc				; return if error
 37029 000064C0 72FA                    	jc	short pJFNFromHandle_error
 37030 000064C2 26803DFF                	CMP     BYTE [ES:DI],-1		; unused handle
 37031                                  	;JNZ	short GetSF		; nope, suck out SF
 37032                                  	;;mov	al,6
 37033                                  	;MOV	AL,error_invalid_handle ; appropriate error
 37034                                  	;jmp	short ReturnCarry	; signal it
 37035                                  	; 17/12/2022
 37036                                  	; 02/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 37037 000064C6 74E9                    	jz	short ReturnCarry_inv_hndl ; Retro DOS v3.0 modification
 37038                                  	;JNZ	short GetSF		; nope, suck out SF
 37039                                  	;;mov	al,6
 37040                                  	;MOV	AL,error_invalid_handle ; appropriate error
 37041                                  	;jmp	short ReturnCarry	; signal it
 37042                                  GetSF:
 37043 000064C8 53                      	push	bx			; save handle
 37044 000064C9 268A1D                  	MOV     BL,[ES:DI]		; get SFN
 37045 000064CC 30FF                    	XOR     BH,BH                   ; ignore upper half
 37046 000064CE E80200                  	CALL    SFFromSFN               ; get real sf spot
 37047 000064D1 5B                      	pop	bx			; restore
 37048 000064D2 C3                      	retn                        	; say goodbye

 37050                                  ;BREAK <SFFromSFN - index into SF table for SFN>
 37051                                  
 37052                                  ;**	SFFromSFN - Get an SF Table entry from an SFN
 37053                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37054                                  ;	SFFromSfn uses an SFN to index an entry into the SF table. This
 37055                                  ;	is more than just a simple index instruction because the SF table
 37056                                  ;	can be made up of multiple pieces chained together. We follow the
 37057                                  ;	chain to the right piece and then do the index operation.
 37058                                  ;
 37059                                  ;   NOTE:
 37060                                  ;	This routine is called from SFFromHandle which is called
 37061                                  ;       at DOSINIT time with SS NOT DOSGROUP
 37062                                  ;
 37063                                  ;	ENTRY	BX has SF index
 37064                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 37065                                  ;		  ES:DI points to SF entry
 37066                                  ;		'C' set if index too large
 37067                                  ;	USES	BX, DI, ES
 37068                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37069                                  
 37070                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37071                                  
 37072                                  SFFromSFN:
 37073                                  	; 05/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 37074                                  	;getdseg <es>			; es -> dosdata
 37075 000064D3 2E8E06[0700]            	mov	es,[cs:DosDSeg]
 37076                                  
 37077                                  	;LES	DI,[CS:SFT_ADDR]	; (es:di) = start of SFT table
 37078 000064D8 26C43E[2A00]            	les	di,[es:SFT_ADDR]
 37079                                  sfsfn5:	
 37080                                  	;cmp	bx,[es:di+4]
 37081 000064DD 263B5D04                	CMP	BX,[ES:DI+SFT.SFCount]	; is handle in this table?
 37082 000064E1 720E                    	JB	short sfsfn7		; yes, go grab it
 37083                                  	;sub	bx,[es:di+4]
 37084 000064E3 262B5D04                	SUB     BX,[ES:DI+SFT.SFCount]
 37085 000064E7 26C43D                  	les	di,[es:di] ; 14/08/2018
 37086                                  	;LES	DI,[ES:DI+SFT.SFLink]	; get next table segment
 37087 000064EA 83FFFF                  	CMP     DI,-1                   ; end of tables?
 37088 000064ED 75EE                    	JNZ	short sfsfn5		; no, try again
 37089 000064EF F9                      	STC
 37090 000064F0 C3                      	retn				; return with error, not found
 37091                                  sfsfn7:
 37092 000064F1 50                      	push	ax
 37093                                  	;mov	ax,53 ; MSDOS 3.3
 37094                                  	;mov	ax,59 ; MSDOS 6.0
 37095                                  	;MOV	AX,SF_ENTRY.size	; put it in a nice place
 37096                                  	
 37097                                  	; 17/12/2022
 37098 000064F2 B03B                    	mov	al,SF_ENTRY.size ; 28/05/2019
 37099                                  	; 07/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 37100                                  	;mov	ax,SF_ENTRY.size ; 59
 37101                                  	
 37102 000064F4 F6E3                    	MUL	BL			; (ax) = offset into this SF block
 37103 000064F6 01C7                    	ADD	DI,AX			; add base of SF block
 37104 000064F8 58                      	pop	ax
 37105                                  	;add	di,6
 37106 000064F9 83C706                  	ADD	DI,SFT.SFTable		; offset into structure, 'C' cleared
 37107 000064FC C3                      	retn				; return with 'C' clear

 37111                                  ;**	JFNFree - Find a Free JFN Slot
 37112                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37113                                  ;	JFNFree scansthrough the JFN table and returnsa pointer to a free slot
 37114                                  ;
 37115                                  ;	ENTRY	(ss) = DOSDATA
 37116                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 37117                                  ;		  (bx) = new handle
 37118                                  ;		  (es:di) = pointer to JFN slot
 37119                                  ;		'C' set if error
 37120                                  ;		  (al) = error code
 37121                                  ;	USES	bx, di, es, flags
 37122                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37123                                  
 37124                                  JFNFree:
 37125 000064FD 31DB                    	XOR	BX,BX			; (bx) = initial JFN to try
 37126                                  jfnf1:	
 37127 000064FF E89EFF                  	CALL	pJFNFromHandle		; get the appropriate handle
 37128 00006502 7209                    	JC	short jfnf5		; no more handles
 37129 00006504 26803DFF                	CMP     BYTE [ES:DI],-1		; free?
 37130 00006508 7405                    	je	short jfnfx		; yes, carry is clear
 37131 0000650A 43                      	INC     BX                      ; no, next handle
 37132 0000650B EBF2                    	JMP	short jfnf1		; and try again
 37133                                  
 37134                                  	; Error. 'C' set
 37135                                  jfnf5:	
 37136                                  	;mov	al,4
 37137 0000650D B004                    	MOV	AL,error_too_many_open_files
 37138                                  jfnfx:	
 37139 0000650F C3                      	retn				; bye
 37140                                  
 37141                                  ;	BREAK <SFNFree - Allocate a free SFN>
 37142                                  
 37143                                  ;**	SFNFree - Allocate a Free SFN/SFT
 37144                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37145                                  ;	SFNFree scans through the sf table looking for a free entry
 37146                                  ;	If it finds one it partially allocates it by setting SFT_REF_COUNT = -1
 37147                                  ;
 37148                                  ;	The problem is that we want to mark the SFT busy so that other threads
 37149                                  ;	can't allocate the SFT before we're finished marking it up.  However,
 37150                                  ;	we can't just mark it busy because we may get blown out of our open
 37151                                  ;	by INT24 and leave the thing orphaned.	To solve this we mark it
 37152                                  ;	"allocation in progress" by setting SFT_REF_COUNT = -1.  If we see
 37153                                  ;	an SFT with this value we look to see if it belongs to this user
 37154                                  ;	and process.  If it does belong to us then it must be an orphan
 37155                                  ;	and we reclaim it.
 37156                                  ;
 37157                                  ;	BUGBUG - improve the performance. I guess it's smaller to call SFFromSFN
 37158                                  ;		over and over, but we could at least set a high water mark...
 37159                                  ;		cause an N^2 loop calling slow SFFromSFN is real slow, too slow
 37160                                  ;		even though this is not a frequently called routine - jgl
 37161                                  ;
 37162                                  ;	ENTRY	(ss) = DOSDATA
 37163                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if no error
 37164                                  ;		  (bx) = SFN
 37165                                  ;		  (es:di) = pointer to SFT
 37166                                  ;		  es:[di].SFT_REF_COUNT = -1
 37167                                  ;		'C' set if error
 37168                                  ;		  (al) = error code
 37169                                  ;	USES	bx, di, es, Flags
 37170                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37171                                  
 37172                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37173                                  	; DOSCODE:A682h (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37174                                  
 37175                                  SFNFree:
 37176                                  	; 12/08/2018
 37177                                  	; 05/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 37178                                  	;
 37179                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 37180 00006510 50                      	push	ax
 37181 00006511 31DB                    	xor	bx,bx			; (bx) = SFN to consider
 37182                                  sfnf5:	
 37183 00006513 53                      	push	bx
 37184 00006514 E8BCFF                  	call	SFFromSFN		; get the potential handle
 37185 00006517 5B                      	pop	bx
 37186 00006518 723A                    	jc	short sfnf95		; no more free SFNs
 37187 0000651A 26833D00                	cmp	word [ES:DI],0
 37188                                  	;cmp	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_Ref_Count],0 ; free?
 37189 0000651E 741D                    	je	short sfnf20			; yep, got one
 37190                                  	
 37191                                  	;cmp	word [es:di],0FFFFh ; -1
 37192 00006520 26833DFF                	cmp	word [ES:DI],sf_busy
 37193                                  	;cmp	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count],sf_busy
 37194 00006524 7403                    	je	short sfnf10		; special busy mark
 37195                                  sfnf7:	
 37196 00006526 43                      	inc	bx			; try the next one
 37197 00006527 EBEA                    	jmp	short sfnf5
 37198                                  
 37199                                  ;	The SFT has the special "busy" mark; if it belongs to us then
 37200                                  ;	it was abandoned during a earlier call and we can use it.
 37201                                  ;
 37202                                  ;	(bx)	= SFN
 37203                                  ;	(es:di) = pointer to SFT
 37204                                  ;	(TOS)	= caller's (ax)
 37205                                  
 37206                                  sfnf10:	
 37207 00006529 36A1[3E03]              	mov	ax,[SS:USER_ID]
 37208                                  	;cmp	[es:di+2Fh],ax
 37209 0000652D 2639452F                	cmp	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_UID],ax
 37210 00006531 75F3                    	jnz	short sfnf7		; not ours
 37211 00006533 36A1[3C03]              	mov	ax,[SS:PROC_ID]
 37212                                  	;cmp	[es:di+31h],ax
 37213 00006537 26394531                	cmp	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_PID],ax
 37214 0000653B 75E9                    	jnz	short sfnf7		; can't use this one, try the next
 37215                                  
 37216                                  ;	We have an SFT to allocate
 37217                                  ;
 37218                                  ;	(bx)	= SFN
 37219                                  ;	(es:di) = pointer to SFT
 37220                                  ;	(TOS)	= caller's (ax)
 37221                                  
 37222                                  sfnf20:
 37223                                  	; cf = 0 ;; Retro DOS v3.0
 37224                                  
 37225                                  	;mov	word [es:di],0FFFFh
 37226 0000653D 26C705FFFF              	mov	word [ES:DI],sf_busy
 37227                                  					; make sure that this is allocated
 37228                                  	;mov	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count],sf_busy
 37229                                  
 37230 00006542 36A1[3E03]              	mov	ax,[SS:USER_ID]
 37231                                  	;mov	[es:di+2Fh],ax
 37232 00006546 2689452F                	mov	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_UID],ax
 37233 0000654A 36A1[3C03]              	mov	ax,[SS:PROC_ID]
 37234                                  	;mov	[es:di+31h],ax
 37235 0000654E 26894531                	mov	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_PID],ax
 37236                                  sfnf21: ;; Retro DOS v3.0
 37237                                  	; 02/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 37238                                  	;pop	ax
 37239                                  	;;clc
 37240                                  	;retn				; return with no error
 37241                                  	; 17/12/2022
 37242 00006552 58                      	pop	ax
 37243                                  	;clc
 37244 00006553 C3                      	retn
 37245                                  
 37246                                  ;**	Error - no more free SFNs
 37247                                  ;
 37248                                  ;	'C' set

 37252 00006554 58                      	pop	ax

 37255                                  %if 0

 37268                                  ; 20/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 37269                                  
 37270                                  ; DOSCODE:A72Bh (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 37271                                  
 37272                                  ;	BREAK <$Close - return a handle to the system>
 37273                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37274                                  ;
 37275                                  ;**	$Close - Close a file Handle
 37276                                  ;
 37277                                  ;	BUGBUG - close gets called a LOT with invalid handles - sizzle that
 37278                                  ;		path
 37279                                  ;
 37280                                  ;	Assembler usage:
 37281                                  ;	    MOV     BX, handle
 37282                                  ;	    MOV     AH, Close
 37283                                  ;	    INT     int_command
 37284                                  ;
 37285                                  ;	ENTRY	(bx) = handle
 37286                                  ;	EXIT	<normal INT21 return convention>
 37287                                  ;	USES	all
 37288                                  ;
 37289                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37290                                  
 37291                                  ; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37292                                  ; DOSCODE:A6CBh (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37293                                  
 37294                                  _$CLOSE:
 37295                                  ;	Grab the SFT pointer from the JFN.
 37296                                  
 37297 00006557 E84802                  	call	CheckOwner		; get system file entry
 37298 0000655A 722B                    	jc	short CloseError	; error return
 37299 0000655C 16                      	push	ss
 37300 0000655D 1F                      	pop	ds			; For DOS_CLOSE
 37301 0000655E 893E[9E05]              	MOV	[THISSFT],DI		; save offset of pointer
 37302 00006562 8C06[A005]              	MOV	[THISSFT+2],ES		; save segment value
 37303                                  
 37304                                  ; DS:SI point to JFN table entry.
 37305                                  ; ES:DI point to SFT
 37306                                  ;
 37307                                  ; We now examine the user's JFN entry; If the file was a 70-mode file (network
 37308                                  ; FCB, we examine the ref count on the SFT; if it was 1, we free the JFN.

 37778                                  	ADD	AX,BX			; get new segment
 37779                                  	MOV	DS,AX			; in seg register

 37783                                  						;smr;SS Override
 37784                                  	retn

 38150                                  ;Break	<CheckOwner - verify ownership of handles from server>
 38151                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 38152                                  ;   CheckOwner - Due to the ability of the server to close file handles for a
 38153                                  ;   process without the process knowing it (delete/rename of open files, for
 38154                                  ;   example), it is possible for the redirector to issue a call to a handle
 38155                                  ;   that it soes not rightfully own. We check here to make sure that the
 38156                                  ;   issuing process is the owner of the SFT. At the same time, we do a
 38157                                  ;   SFFromHandle to really make sure that the SFT is good.
 38158                                  ;
 38159                                  ;	ENTRY	BX has the handle
 38160                                  ;		User_ID is the current user
 38161                                  ;	EXIT	Carry Clear => ES:DI points to SFT
 38162                                  ;		Carry Set => AX has error code
 38163                                  ;	USES	none
 38164                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 38165                                  
 38166                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 38167                                  	; 21/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 38168                                  CheckOwner:
 38169                                  	; 13/07/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 38170                                  
 38171 000067A2 E818FD                  	call	SFFromHandle
 38172 000067A5 721B                    	jc	short co_ret_label	; retc
 38173                                  
 38174 000067A7 50                      	push	ax
 38175                                  
 38176                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 38177

 38179                                  ;SR; are shared across multiple VMs in win386.

 38183 000067B0 31C0                    	xor	ax,ax			;set the zero flag

 38185

 38192 000067BC 58                      	pop	ax

 38214                                  ;	TITLE	MACRO - Pathname and macro related internal routines
 38215                                  ;	NAME	MACRO
 38216                                  
 38217                                  ;	Microsoft Confidential
 38218                                  ;	Copyright (C) Microsoft Corporation 1991
 38219                                  ;	All Rights Reserved.
 38220                                  
 38221                                  ;**	MACRO.ASM
 38222                                  ;
 38223                                  ;	$AssignOper
 38224                                  ;	FIND_DPB
 38225                                  ;	InitCDS
 38226                                  ;	$UserOper
 38227                                  ;	GetVisDrv
 38228                                  ;	GetThisDrv
 38229                                  ;	GetCDSFromDrv
 38230                                  ;
 38231                                  ;   Revision history:
 38232                                  ;
 38233                                  ;	Created: MZ 4 April 1983
 38234                                  ;		 MZ 18 April 1983   Make TransFCB handle extended FCBs
 38235                                  ;		 AR 2 June 1983     Define/Delete macro for NET redir.
 38236                                  ;		 MZ 3 Nov 83	    Fix InitCDS to reset length to 2
 38237                                  ;		 MZ 4 Nov 83	    Fix NetAssign to use STRLEN only
 38238                                  ;		 MZ 18 Nov 83	    Rewrite string processing for subtree
 38239                                  ;				    aliasing.
 38240                                  ;
 38241                                  ;   MSDOS performs several types of name translation. First, we maintain for
 38242                                  ;   each valid drive letter the text of the current directory on that drive.
 38243                                  ;   For invalid drive letters, there is no current directory so we pretend to
 38244                                  ;   be at the root. A current directory is either the raw local directory
 38245                                  ;   (consisting of drive:\path) or a local network directory (consisting of
 38246                                  ;   \\machine\path. There is a limit on the point to which a .. is allowed.
 38247                                  ;
 38248                                  ;   Given a path, MSDOS will transform this into a real from-the-root path
 38249                                  ;   without . or .. entries. Any component that is > 8.3 is truncated to
 38250                                  ;   this and all * are expanded into ?'s.
 38251                                  ;
 38252                                  ;   The second part of name translation involves subtree aliasing. A list of
 38253                                  ;   subtree pairs is maintained by the external utility SUBST. The results of
 38254                                  ;   the previous 'canonicalization' are then examined to see if any of the
 38255                                  ;   subtree pairs is a prefix of the user path. If so, then this prefix is
 38256                                  ;   replaced with the other subtree in the pair.
 38257                                  ;
 38258                                  ;   A third part involves mapping this "real" path into a "physical" path.  A
 38259                                  ;   list of drive/subtree pairs are maintained by the external utility JOIN.
 38260                                  ;   The output of the previous translation is examined to see if any of the
 38261                                  ;   subtrees in this list are a prefix of the string. If so, then the prefix
 38262                                  ;   is replaced by the appropriate drive letter. In this manner, we can
 38263                                  ;   'mount' one device under another.
 38264                                  ;
 38265                                  ;   The final form of name translation involves the mapping of a user's
 38266                                  ;   logical drive number into the internal physical drive. This is
 38267                                  ;   accomplished by converting the drive number into letter:CON, performing
 38268                                  ;   the above translation and then converting the character back into a drive
 38269                                  ;   number.
 38270                                  ;
 38271                                  ;   There are two main entry points: TransPath and TransFCB. TransPath will
 38272                                  ;   take a path and form the real text of the pathname with all . and ..
 38273                                  ;   removed. TransFCB will translate an FCB into a path and then invoke
 38274                                  ;   TransPath.
 38275                                  ;
 38276                                  ;	A000	version 4.00  Jan. 1988
 38277                                  
 38278                                  ;Installed = TRUE
 38279                                  
 38280                                  ;	I_need	ThisCDS,DWORD		; pointer to CDS used
 38281                                  ;	I_need	CDSAddr,DWORD		; pointer to CDS table
 38282                                  ;	I_need	CDSCount,BYTE		; number of CDS entries
 38283                                  ;	I_need	CurDrv,BYTE		; current macro assignment (old
 38284                                  ;					; current drive)
 38285                                  ;	I_need	NUMIO,BYTE		; Number of physical drives
 38286                                  ;	I_need	fSharing,BYTE		; TRUE => no redirection allowed
 38287                                  ;	I_need	DummyCDS,80h		; buffer for dummy cds
 38288                                  ;	I_need	DIFFNAM,BYTE		; flag for MyName being set
 38289                                  ;	I_need	MYNAME,16		; machine name
 38290                                  ;	I_need	MYNUM,WORD		; machine number
 38291                                  ;	I_need	DPBHEAD,DWORD		; beginning of DPB chain

 38869                                  ;BREAK <TransPath - copy a path, do string sub and put in current dir>
 38870                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 38871                                  ;
 38872                                  ;   TransPath - copy a path from DS:SI to ES:DI, performing component string
 38873                                  ;       substitution, insertion of current directory and fixing . and ..
 38874                                  ;       entries. Perform splicing. Allow input string to match splice
 38875                                  ;       exactly.
 38876                                  ;
 38877                                  ;   TransPathSet - Same as above except No splicing is performed if input path
 38878                                  ;       matches splice.
 38879                                  ;
 38880                                  ;   TransPathNoSet - No splicing/local using is performed at all.
 38881                                  ;
 38882                                  ;   The following anomalous behaviour is required:
 38883                                  ;
 38884                                  ;       Drive letters on devices are ignored. (set up DummyCDS)
 38885                                  ;       Paths on devices are ignored. (truncate to 0-length)
 38886                                  ;       Raw net I/O sets ThisCDS => NULL.
 38887                                  ;       fSharing => dummyCDS and no subst/splice. Only canonicalize.
 38888                                  ;
 38889                                  ;   Other behaviour:
 38890                                  ;
 38891                                  ;       ThisCDS set up.
 38892                                  ;       FatRead done on local CDS.
 38893                                  ;       ValidateCDS done on local CDS.
 38894                                  ;
 38895                                  ;   Brief flowchart:
 38896                                  ;
 38897                                  ;       if fSharing then
 38898                                  ;           set up DummyCDS (ThisCDS)
 38899                                  ;           canonicalize (sets cMeta)
 38900                                  ;           splice
 38901                                  ;           fatRead
 38902                                  ;           return
 38903                                  ;       if \\ or d:\\ lead then
 38904                                  ;           set up null CDS (ThisCDS)
 38905                                  ;           canonicalize (sets cMeta)
 38906                                  ;           return
 38907                                  ;       if device then
 38908                                  ;           set up dummyCDS (ThisCDS)
 38909                                  ;           canonicalize (sets cMeta)
 38910                                  ;           return
 38911                                  ;       if file then
 38912                                  ;           getCDS (sets (ThisCDS) from name)
 38913                                  ;           validateCDS (may reset current dir)
 38914                                  ;           Copy current dir
 38915                                  ;           canonicalize (set cMeta)
 38916                                  ;           splice
 38917                                  ;           generate correct CDS (ThisCDS)
 38918                                  ;           if local then
 38919                                  ;               fatread
 38920                                  ;           return
 38921                                  ;
 38922                                  ;   Inputs:     DS:SI - point to ASCIZ string path
 38923                                  ;               DI - point to buffer in DOSDATA
 38924                                  ;   Outputs:    Carry Set - invalid path specification: too many .., bad
 38925                                  ;                   syntax, etc. or user FAILed to I 24.
 38926                                  ;               WFP_Start - points to beginning of buffer
 38927                                  ;               Curr_Dir_End - points to end of current dir in path
 38928                                  ;               DS - DOSDATA
 38929                                  ;   Registers modified: most
 38930                                  ;
 38931                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 38932                                  
 38933                                  ; 22/05/2019
 38934                                  ; 13/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 38935                                  ; DOSCODE:AB99h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 38936                                  
 38937                                  ; 04/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 38938                                  ; DOSCODE:AB39h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)

 39587                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 39588                                  ;   Splice - take a string and substitute a prefix if one exists. Change
 39589                                  ;       ThisCDS to point to physical drive CDS.
